body.p: Claims 1-6 and 8-18 are pending in this application. The various parts of the Office Action (and other matters, if any) are discussed below under appropriate headings.

Claims 1-6 and 8-16 stand rejected as anticipated by U.S. 2017/0245776 ("Kurtz"). Claims 17 and 18 stand rejected as unpatentable over Kurtz in view of U.S. 2013/0204155 ("Brull"). Applicant asks the Examiner to reconsider and withdraw the rejection(s) for at least the following reasons.
Claim 1 has been amended to include the subject matter of claims 17 and 18. Consequently, the rejection of amended claim 1 is discussed below in view of the rejection of claims 17 and 18.
Independent Claim 1

Amended claim 1 recites a "method performed by an anesthetizing monitoring unit configured to generate an improved evoked electromyography response signalSVG {EMBED HERE} 0.160.797 The method "generat[es] a single stimuli signal (SstimuIi) using theanesthetizing monitoring unit." The "single stimuli signal (SstimuIi) comprises a single pulse and is configured to stimulate a motor nerve of a patient."

The method "output[s] the generated single stimuli signal (Sstimuii) to stimulating electrodes on the patient using an output port of the anesthetizing monitoring unit." The method also "receiv[es] a single evoked electromyography, EMG, response signal (SResponse) from receiving electrodes on the patient at an input port of the anesthetizing monitoring unit, having a duration (TResponse), in response to the transmitted stimuli signal (SstimuIi)." The method "estimat[es] a periodic noise waveform (SPeriodic), having the duration (TResponse), by using temporal segments of a noise signal (SNoise)."
The "temporal segments of the noise signal (SNoise) used during the estimating of the periodic noise waveform (SPeriodic) are detected during a time interval (TNoise) not

Analysis: Amended Claim 1 Rejection

The cited reference combination does not disclose -as set forth in amended claim 1- "estimating a periodic noise waveform (SPeriodic), having the duration (TResponse), by using temporal segments of a noise signal (SNoise)."

In the Office Action, the Examiner points to Brull as disclosing amended claim 1's estimating a periodic noise waveform. In particular, the Examiner points to Brull, paragraph 0022, which reads as follows:
"For purposes of determining the amplitude of the evoked muscle

response, the start of the evoked muscle response is optio SVG {EMBED HERE} 0.5031.073 SVG {EMBED HERE} 0.2871.10by locating the time at which the level of muscle electrical a the f electrical noise in the subject prior to s the immediately following completion of the evoked
response. The baseline level of electrical noise is the background noise
and may include all ambient, intrinsic and extrinsic noise. The amplitude is
determined as the difference in measured voltage from the baseline level
to the positive or negative peak of the evoked muscle response caused by
stimulating the motor nerve." (Emphasis added.)

Brull does not disclose estimating a periodic noise waveform using temporal segments of a noise signal. While Brull mentions a baseline noise level in paragraph 0022, Brull is silent regarding how this baseline noise level is determined. At most, Brull describes determining an amplitude value, but is silent regarding estimating a periodic noise waveform.

As argued in the previous rejection, Kurtz teaches averaging multiple responses SResponse received during the time period TResponse. That is, Kurtz describes receiving multiple responses including noise and signal, and averaging these responses. Kurtz is silent regarding a waveform.
RESPONSE5

Additionally, it is not clear how Brull can be applied to Kurtz. If Brull and Kurtz were combined, the resulting method would not calculate an aggregated amplitude value from RESPONSE 1-5 and then subtract a fixed level or value representing noise from that aggregated amplitude value.
In the claimed subject matter, the noise is determined as waveforms in the period "between" a stimuli pulse and a response signal RESPONSE 1-5. As can be seen from

This improves each individual response signal compared to Kurtz's aggregating the compounded measurements of noise and signal. That is, an improved amplitude value of the response signal is generated for each response signal.

This further reduces the delay in amplitude values compared to Kurtz, where all of the multiple time-based data series needs to be obtained before processing by weighted average can be performed. Further, the present disclosure has the advantage of better performance when the assumption of quasi-stationary noise over the period of the weighted averaging is not true. The present disclosure then adapts to the noise at each received response SResponse.
For at least the above reason, the cited reference combination does not disclose the subject matter of amended claim 1. Withdrawal of the rejection is respectfully requested.
